papers.title: Exploration and experimental validation of oxidative stress-related diagnostic genes in interstitial cystitis based on transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Interstitial cystitis (IC) is a chronic pain syndrome with an elusive diagnosis and poorly understood pathogenesis, in which oxidative stress (OS) is increasingly implicated. This study aimed to identify and validate OS-related diagnostic biomarkers for IC using an integrative computational and experimental approach.
papers.summary: This study identifies and validates oxidative stress-related genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers for interstitial cystitis (IC), a chronic pain condition with unclear causes. Using transcriptomic data and experimental validation, the authors pinpoint specific genes that could help diagnose IC and shed light on its pathogenesis.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) comprises a group of rare inherited genodermatoses characterized by fragility and blistering of the skin and mucous membranes, chronic wounding, and significant morbidity including increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma in severe subtypes. Key unmet priorities include reducing diagnostic latency, establishing objective wound monitoring, enabling early detection of malignant transformation within chronic ulcerations, and developing therapies that durably modify disease progression. Artificial intelligence (AI) encompassing machine learning (ML), and deep learning (
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly machine and deep learning, could address key challenges in inherited epidermolysis bullosa (EB), such as faster diagnosis, objective wound monitoring, and early cancer detection. The authors discuss current evidence and future directions for AI applications in this rare skin disease.

papers.title: In Silico Prioritisation of Similarity-Selected Small Molecules Targeting the IsdB NEAT Domain of Staphylococcus aureus as a Potential Antivirulence Strategy.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has necessitated the development of alternative therapeutic strategies targeting bacterial virulence factors. This study employed an integrated in silico approach to identifying potential inhibitors of the iron-regulated surface determinant B Near-iron Transporter domain, a key protein involved in heme acquisition and pathogenicity. Virtual screening and molecular docking identified certain similarity-selected small molecules possessing strong binding affinities, with (4-(1-oxoisoindolin-2-yl)benzoic acid (TOP1) and
papers.summary: This study used computer simulations to identify small molecules that might block a key protein (IsdB NEAT domain) used by MRSA to steal iron from human hosts, offering a potential new way to fight antibiotic-resistant infections without directly killing the bacteria. The top candidate, TOP1, showed strong predicted binding to the target protein.

papers.title: Quantum convolutional HLA immunogenic peptide prediction (Q-CHIPP): Next-generation neoantigen prediction with quantum neural network.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of quantum computing is driven by promises of performing complex calculations with unprecedented speed; however, current use cases have been limited by quantum hardware and the difficulty of identifying problems that classical computers cannot easily address. Within these constraints, biological problems including drug discovery, protein folding, and precision medicine present an opportunity to understand how current quantum hardware can make advances. In immunology, accurate prediction of cancer neoantigens remains a major challenge, limited by small, noisy datasets and the i
papers.summary: This paper introduces Q-CHIPP, a quantum convolutional neural network for predicting immunogenic peptides (neoantigens) from HLA molecules, aiming to leverage quantum computing's potential for complex biological problems. The method addresses challenges like small, noisy datasets in cancer immunology, though practical quantum hardware limitations remain. It represents an early exploration of quantum machine learning for precision medicine and neoantigen prediction.

papers.title: Antidiabetic potential of a novel hydroxyphenyl-bi-benzopyran-hexol compound from Cassia fistula as an α-amylase inhibitor: Integrated in silico screening and in vitro validation using a nonlinear regression model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a critically important metabolic disease, causing persistent hyperglycemia. Blood glucose levels can be effectively maintained by inhibiting the activity of α-amylase. α-amylase inhibitors manage postprandial hyperglycemia by delaying carbohydrate digestion.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel compound from Cassia fistula that inhibits α-amylase, an enzyme involved in carbohydrate digestion, potentially helping manage blood sugar levels in diabetes. The researchers used computer modeling and lab experiments to validate the compound's activity, with nonlinear regression analysis confirming its effectiveness.

papers.title: DeorphaNN: Virtual screening of GPCR peptide agonists using AlphaFold-predicted active-state complexes and deep learning embeddings.
papers.abstract: Peptide-activated G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) regulate physiological processes through interaction with neuropeptides and peptide hormones. Identifying endogenous peptide agonists remains challenging, as peptide-GPCR pairings often follow gene-family relationships that offer limited predictive insight for orphan GPCRs without characterized homologs. Using a dataset of experimentally validated peptide-GPCR interactions from Caenorhabditis elegans, we demonstrate that AF-multimer confidence metrics partially discriminate agonist from non-agonist complexes, with improved discrimination us
papers.summary: This paper introduces DeorphaNN, a method that combines AlphaFold-predicted active-state GPCR structures with deep learning embeddings to identify peptide agonists for orphan GPCRs. Using C. elegans data, they show that AlphaFold confidence metrics can partially distinguish agonist from non-agonist complexes, and their approach improves prediction accuracy for peptide-GPCR pairings.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational characterization of bioactive metabolites from Streptomyces paradoxus GH53 with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antitumor activities.
papers.abstract: Streptomyces species are widely recognized as valuable sources of secondary metabolites with diverse biological activities. In this study, the isolate GH53 was identified as Streptomyces paradoxus based on morphological characteristics and partial 16 S rRNA gene sequence analysis. Fermentation conditions were optimized to enhance metabolite production, and the crude ethyl acetate extract was chemically characterized using GC-MS, FT-IR, and UV-Vis spectroscopy. The analytical profile suggested the presence of a chemically complex mixture containing fatty acids, fatty acid derivatives, hydrocarb
papers.summary: This study identifies a Streptomyces paradoxus strain that produces a complex mixture of bioactive metabolites with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antitumor activities, characterized through experimental and computational methods. The findings highlight the potential of this bacterial strain as a source of natural products for drug discovery.

papers.title: Mol2Image: an enhanced DDI prediction framework leveraging drug molecular descriptors.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are a critical safety issue in clinical practice, as they can lead to severe and often unpredictable adverse effects. This risk becomes significantly higher in multi-drug therapies, which are increasingly used in the treatment of complex and chronic diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular disorders, and diabetes. However, identifying DDIs through in vivo studies is costly and time-consuming. In this study, a novel DDI prediction model, Mol2Image, has been proposed that utilizes chemical structure features derived from Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (
papers.summary: Mol2Image is a new computational model that predicts drug-drug interactions by converting chemical structure data into image-like representations, enabling more efficient and accurate identification of potential adverse effects without costly lab experiments.

papers.title: Methods for the establishment of enzymatic mechanisms - from QM to ML.
papers.abstract: We offer a practical and conceptual introduction to some of the current approaches to modelling enzymatic reaction mechanisms, ranging from quantum mechanics (QM), molecular mechanics (MM), and hybrid QM/MM approaches to enhanced sampling methods, knowledge-based approaches, and machine learning (ML) advances. We discuss how static and dynamic QM/MM approaches, as well as multi-PES strategies, have contributed to understanding the role of conformational diversity, electrostatic preorganization and solvent participation in the determination of catalytic barriers and reaction paths. We focus on
papers.summary: This review provides a practical introduction to computational methods for modeling enzymatic reaction mechanisms, covering quantum mechanics, molecular mechanics, hybrid QM/MM approaches, enhanced sampling, and machine learning. It explains how these techniques have revealed the roles of conformational diversity, electrostatic preorganization, and solvent participation in catalysis.

papers.title: AI-driven computational drug design: tools, workflow and challenges.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery is a time-consuming and resource-intensive process with a development period of more than ten years and a clinical attrition rate of more than 90%. Despite its contributions to rational drug design, computer-aided drug design has been constrained by limited scalability, overreliance on molecular descriptors, and incomplete modeling of complex biological systems. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed this landscape. AI-based drug discovery platforms have shifted the paradigm from a narrow focus to a comprehensive platform that covers target identification
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI is transforming drug discovery by overcoming limitations of traditional computer-aided design, such as poor scalability and incomplete biological modeling. AI-based platforms now offer comprehensive workflows covering target identification and beyond, potentially reducing the long timelines and high failure rates of drug development.

papers.title: AI-Driven discovery and experimental validation of covalent FGFR4 inhibitors for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: FGFR4 signaling is an essential driver in hepatocellular carcinoma. However, traditional screening is often time-consuming, highlighting a need for efficient strategies to identify covalent chemotypes and accelerate FGFR4 drug discovery.
papers.summary: This study uses AI to discover and experimentally validate new covalent inhibitors of FGFR4, a key driver in liver cancer. The AI-driven approach identified promising drug candidates faster than traditional screening methods, offering a more efficient path to developing targeted therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: Rapid and energy-efficient ultra-large library screening for drug discovery on a SpiNNaker2 neuromorphic chip.
papers.abstract: The virtual screening of make-on-demand small molecule libraries can prioritize drug candidates for rapid experimental validation to accelerate pre-clinical drug discovery. As ultra-large libraries grow to billions of compounds, exhaustive screening incurs prohibitive costs and energy consumption. We address this challenge with the neuromorphic SpiNNaker2 system, designed for massively parallel AI tasks. Here, we show the implementation of a ligand-based screening pipeline on a 152-core SpiNNaker2 chip. We adapted feed-forward neural networks trained on 2D molecular descriptors to screen 19 bi
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates the use of a SpiNNaker2 neuromorphic chip to perform ultra-large virtual screening of drug-like molecules with high energy efficiency. By implementing ligand-based neural networks on a 152-core chip, the authors show that screening billions of compounds can be done rapidly and with drastically reduced power consumption compared to traditional computing. This approach could make exhaustive screening of make-on-demand libraries practical for early-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: AlphaDTA: integrating AlphaFold3 embeddings and 3D complex structures for drug-target binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target binding affinity plays an important role in structure-based drug discovery, yet existing approaches are constrained by their reliance on scarce experimentally determined protein-ligand complex structures. In this context, recent advances in biomolecular structure prediction models, such as AlphaFold3, have emerged as a promising approach to alleviate the scarcity of experimentally determined protein-ligand complex structures. In this study, we introduce AlphaDTA, a framework that integrates AlphaFold3-predicted structures and embeddings for drug-target bindin
papers.summary: AlphaDTA is a new computational framework that uses AlphaFold3-predicted protein structures and embeddings to predict how strongly a drug binds to its target, overcoming the problem of limited experimental data. By integrating these predicted 3D complex structures, the method improves drug-target binding affinity predictions for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Emetine dihydrochloride inhibits Chikungunya virus nsP2 helicase and shows robust antiviral activity in cells and mice.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a mosquito-borne alphavirus, causes frequent global epidemics of chikungunya fever, characterized by severe joint pain and debilitating arthritis. With no specific antiviral therapies available, these outbreaks pose a major public health challenge, particularly in tropical regions. There is thus urgent need to develop novel antivirals. Drug repurposing is an attractive strategy to identify potential antivirals targeting CHIKV replication.
papers.summary: This study identifies emetine dihydrochloride, an FDA-approved anti-protozoal drug, as a potent inhibitor of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replication by targeting the viral nsP2 helicase. The drug showed strong antiviral activity in cell culture and in a mouse model, suggesting it could be repurposed as a treatment for CHIKV infections.

papers.title: In silico study: ADMET-driven pharmacokinetic profiling of antiviral compounds for pre-clinical screening framework of intranasal drug development.
papers.abstract: The ongoing emergence of respiratory viral pathogens, including novel variants and established threats such as influenza, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), continues to challenge global health systems due to limited specific therapeutic options. Intranasal antiviral delivery represents a promising approach for targeting respiratory tract infections; however, drug development frequently fails due to inappropriate pharmacokinetic properties. This study employed computational ADMET Predictor tools to systematically evaluate the ph
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacological and toxicological methods
papers.summary: This study used computational ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) prediction tools to evaluate the pharmacokinetic properties of antiviral compounds for intranasal drug development, aiming to identify promising candidates early and reduce late-stage failures. The in silico framework provides a pre-clinical screening approach to prioritize compounds with favorable drug-like properties for respiratory viral infections.

papers.title: Enhancing virtual screening of cystathionine β-synthase inhibitors: benchmarking target-specific machine-learning scoring functions against state-of-the-art AI docking and co-folding approaches.
papers.abstract: Cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) has emerged as an important therapeutic target implicated in cancer and Down syndrome, yet the discovery of selective CBS inhibitors remains challenging due to limited structural diversity of known ligands and the scarcity of target-focused virtual screening (VS) benchmarks. In this study, we present the first comprehensive evaluation of CBS-specific artificial intelligence (AI) models for structure-based VS, supported by a carefully curated and up-to-date data set of experimentally validated CBS inhibitors, true inactives and decoys. Using this data set, we deve
papers.summary: This study presents the first comprehensive evaluation of AI models for virtual screening of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) inhibitors, using a curated dataset of experimentally validated compounds. The authors benchmark target-specific machine-learning scoring functions against state-of-the-art AI docking and co-folding approaches, providing a valuable resource for CBS drug discovery.

papers.title: A lightweight, integrated generative AI assistant for accelerated early-stage drug discovery on constrained-resource hardware.
papers.abstract: Discovery of novel therapeutic small molecules remains one of the most challenging tasks in pharmaceutical research, as it is described by high attrition rates, well over $2 billion per candidate, and timelines often surpassing a decade. Generative AI has transformative potential to probe the enormous chemical space estimated at 1060 drug-like molecules, but current computational approaches are fragmented across multiple tools and require enterprise-grade hardware, thus creating a sort of "computational divide" that excludes many academic groups and smaller laboratories. We introduce in this s
papers.summary: This paper presents a lightweight, integrated generative AI assistant designed to accelerate early-stage drug discovery on constrained-resource hardware, addressing the 'computational divide' that limits access for academic and smaller labs. The tool consolidates multiple computational approaches into a single platform, enabling exploration of vast chemical space without requiring enterprise-grade infrastructure.

papers.title: AI-assisted fragment-based drug discovery of SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain binders validated by NMR and X-ray crystallography.
papers.abstract: Fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) is an effective approach for exploring chemical space using small, low-affinity fragments as starting points to facilitate development of lead compounds. Strategies to improve fragment potency include fragment merging and linking to generate higher-affinity inhibitors. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have accelerated this process through structure-based optimization and generative compound design. Here, we present an AI-assisted FBDD workflow applied to the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain (Mac1), a conserved viral protein involved in
papers.summary: This study presents an AI-assisted fragment-based drug discovery workflow targeting the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain, a conserved viral protein. The approach uses machine learning to optimize fragment merging and linking, leading to higher-affinity inhibitors validated by NMR and X-ray crystallography. This demonstrates how AI can accelerate the early stages of drug discovery for challenging viral targets.

papers.title: X-DILiver: an ensemble learning framework for predicting drug-induced liver injury.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a primary cause of drug attrition, associated with over 1000 medications and accounting for 32% of marketed drugs withdrawn due to toxicity. This has created an urgent demand for high-accuracy computational methods predicting DILI risk early in the drug development pipeline. We developed X-DILiver, a predictive framework built on the largest DILI-annotated dataset to date. We used data augmentation to improve model robustness and address class imbalance. A library of 312 machine learning models was created using various algorithms and molecular features, and
papers.summary: X-DILiver is a new computational framework that predicts drug-induced liver injury (DILI) risk using the largest annotated dataset to date. It employs data augmentation and an ensemble of 312 machine learning models to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, addressing a key need in early drug development.

papers.title: Harnessing data science to control non-communicable diseases in Africa: a systematic review and gap analysis.
papers.abstract: Data science methods can provide novel and pragmatic approaches for preventing and controlling non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Africa. This study highlights current efforts, opportunities, and challenges in leveraging data science methods to accelerate and advance the prevention and control of NCDs in Africa.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how data science methods can be used to prevent and control non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Africa, highlighting current efforts, opportunities, and challenges. The study identifies gaps in the application of these methods and suggests that data science offers novel, pragmatic approaches for addressing NCDs in the region.

papers.title: Integration of molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations identifies a novel flavonoid glycoside as a PCSK9 inhibitor for hypercholesterolemia.
papers.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) significantly influences plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) homeostasis by promoting the degradation of LDL receptors. While monoclonal antibody therapies are effective, their widespread application is limited by high costs and invasive administration, necessitating the development of oral small-molecule inhibitors for hypercholesterolemia management. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of a specific flavonoid glycoside, 7-(alpha-D-Glucopyranosyloxy)-5-hydroxy-2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-4 H-1-benzopyran-4-one, as a novel
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify a flavonoid glycoside as a potential oral small-molecule inhibitor of PCSK9, a key regulator of LDL cholesterol. The compound shows promise as a more accessible alternative to expensive antibody therapies for managing hypercholesterolemia.

papers.title: Evaluation of deep learning architectures for predicting ligand interactions with neurologically relevant GPCRs.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are therapeutic targets for over 30% of approved drugs, yet specific GPCR subtypes act as molecular initiating events in several neurotoxic adverse outcome pathways. Therefore, knowledge of GPCR-ligand interactions is critical for drug discovery and computational toxicology. However, accurate predictions of GPCR-ligand binding can be challenging due to receptor conformational flexibility, complex membrane environment, and lack of selectivity among ligands. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models that jointly encode protein and ligand representations offer a pro
papers.summary: This study evaluates deep learning architectures for predicting how small molecules bind to neurologically relevant GPCRs, a key class of drug targets. The authors compare different models that jointly encode protein and ligand features, aiming to improve accuracy for drug discovery and toxicology applications.

papers.title: EvoDiffMol: evolutionary diffusion framework for 3D molecular design with optimized properties.
papers.abstract: Designing molecules with specific target properties remains a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry. While existing approaches show promise, most rely on simplified representations like SMILES strings or 2D graphs that lack essential three-dimensional geometric information. We present EvoDiffMol, a computational framework that integrates evolutionary algorithms with three-dimensional diffusion models for property-driven molecular generation. The method operates through adaptive evolutionary optimization, where population-based selection guides the generation process toward desired p
papers.summary: EvoDiffMol combines evolutionary algorithms with 3D diffusion models to generate molecules with optimized properties, overcoming the limitations of methods that rely on simplified 2D representations. The framework uses population-based selection to guide molecular generation toward desired characteristics while preserving essential three-dimensional geometric information.

papers.title: VITAGRAPH: building a knowledge graph for biologically relevant learning tasks.
papers.abstract: The complexity of human biology poses ongoing challenges, driving global interdisciplinary research. Artificial intelligence has become a powerful tool in computational biology, where graph data structures model entities like protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and gene functional networks. These networks support crucial tasks in network medicine, including gene-disease association prediction, drug repurposing, and polypharmacy side-effect analysis. Reliable machine learning predictions require high-quality data. We present VITAGRAPH, a comprehensive multi-purpose biological knowledge g
papers.summary: VITAGRAPH is a new comprehensive biological knowledge graph designed to support machine learning tasks in network medicine, such as predicting gene-disease associations and drug repurposing. It integrates diverse biological entities and interactions to provide high-quality data for reliable AI predictions.

papers.title: DRIVE: a comprehensive resource deciphering drug-induced transcriptomic and splicing response in cancer cell.
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapy induces complex molecular reprogramming in cancer, driving transcriptome-wide alterations and widespread dysregulation of alternative splicing. Despite these profound changes, there remain limited resources characterizing drug-induced whole-transcriptomic responses in cancer. Furthermore, while aberrant splicing can generate immunogenic neoantigens, existing resources fail to systematically integrate drug perturbations, splicing dynamics, and neoantigen landscapes. To address this gap, the DRIVE database was constructed as a comprehensive resource detailing drug-induced transcr
papers.summary: The DRIVE database is a new resource that catalogs how drugs alter gene expression and splicing in cancer cells, including the potential to generate immunogenic neoantigens. It fills a gap by systematically integrating drug perturbations with splicing dynamics and neoantigen landscapes.

papers.title: Evaluation of Human-Approved Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Against Lactate Dehydrogenase from Theileria annulata.
papers.abstract: BackgroundTheileriosis, a tick-borne disease caused by Theileria annulata, leads to global economic losses in livestock, emphasizing an urgent need for the identification of new therapeutic agents with alternative mechanisms of action due to rising buparvaquone resistance combined with climate-driven spread. T. annulata lactate dehydrogenase (TaLDH) has been selected as a promising target in the current study. As approximately half of the FDA-approved veterinary drugs are shared with human medicine, integrating drug repurposing has gained importance as an emerging strategy for the management o
papers.summary: This study identifies human-approved drugs that may be repurposed to treat theileriosis, a livestock disease caused by Theileria annulata, by targeting the parasite's lactate dehydrogenase enzyme. The work addresses the urgent need for new treatments due to rising resistance to current drugs and climate-driven spread of the disease.

papers.title: Integrated pan-cancer systems biology and structure-based simulation identifies Annona muricata-derived natural scaffolds as putative IDO1 modulators for cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) is a central immunometabolic checkpoint that promotes tumor immune evasion through dysregulated tryptophan metabolism, yet first-generation inhibitors have shown limited clinical efficacy. This study developed an integrated in silico framework combining pan-cancer systems biology, GC-MS phytochemical profiling, QSAR modeling, molecular docking, ADMET prediction, density functional theory, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation, and MM-PBSA analysis to identify Annona muricata-derived putative IDO1 modulators. Analysis of > 20,000 TCGA samples across 33 cancer
papers.summary: This study used a multi-step computational pipeline—including pan-cancer systems biology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify natural compounds from the plant Annona muricata that may modulate the immune checkpoint IDO1, a target for cancer immunotherapy. The approach analyzed over 20,000 TCGA samples across 33 cancer types and found several candidate scaffolds with favorable drug-like properties. These findings suggest that certain plant-derived compounds could serve as leads for developing IDO1 inhibitors, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Decoding cytokine interactions for psoriasis therapy through computational repurposing of antihypertensive drugs.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated skin disorder characterized by excessive inflammation and the overexpression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17 A, and IFN-γ. Despite the availability of targeted therapies, current treatments often entail high costs, limited accessibility, and adverse side effects. Drug repurposing-utilizing approved medications for novel indications-offers a cost-effective strategy to accelerate the development of alternative therapies with established safety profiles. Twelve FDA-approved antihypertensive drugs-including ACE inhibitors, angiote
papers.summary: This study computationally repurposes FDA-approved antihypertensive drugs for psoriasis therapy by analyzing their interactions with key inflammatory cytokines. The findings suggest that certain antihypertensives may modulate cytokine pathways relevant to psoriasis, offering a cost-effective alternative to current treatments.

papers.title: Design and computational evaluation of E-stilbene-bearing 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives as potential tyrosinase inhibitors using DFT, molecular docking and ADMET studies.
papers.abstract: A series of E-stilbene-bearing 1,3,4-oxadiazole derivatives (4a-b and 5a-f) was synthesized via the Mizoroki-Heck reaction and evaluated as inhibitors of tyrosinase, a vital enzyme involved in melanin biosynthesis. The synthesized compounds were structurally confirmed through NMR spectroscopy (1H NMR, 13C NMR), infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and mass spectrometry. Nearly all derivatives exhibited inhibitory effects against tyrosinase with IC50 values ranging from 0.32 ± 0.03 µM to 6.28 ± 0.05 µM. Among them, compounds 5d and 5b illustrated the most significant inhibitory activity, with IC50 va
papers.summary: This study synthesized and tested new E-stilbene-based compounds as potential inhibitors of tyrosinase, an enzyme involved in melanin production. Several compounds showed strong inhibitory activity, with the most potent having IC50 values as low as 0.32 µM, suggesting they could be developed for skin-lightening or anti-browning applications.

papers.title: Unveiling acetamide coupled benzothiazole hydrazones as potential anti-proliferative agents: an experimental and computational approach.
papers.abstract: A series of benzothiazole acetamide hydrazones (8a-p) was synthesized and evaluated for anti-proliferative activity against various human cancer cell lines, including a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (CAPAN-1), a colorectal carcinoma (HCT-116), a leukemia (HL60), a glioblastoma (LN229), a T lymphoblast (Molt-4), a non-small cell lung cancer (NCI-H460), and a B lymphoblast (Z138) cell line. Among the tested derivatives, compounds 8l, 8n, and 8o emerged as lead compounds, exhibiting cytotoxicity across multiple cell lines. Notably, compound 8o demonstrated selective cytotoxicity towards Z138 a
papers.summary: Researchers synthesized a series of benzothiazole acetamide hydrazones and tested them against seven human cancer cell lines, identifying three lead compounds (8l, 8n, 8o) with broad anti-proliferative activity. One compound (8o) showed selective cytotoxicity against a B lymphoblast cell line, suggesting potential for targeted cancer therapy.

papers.title: Graph-based drug-target interaction modeling: from representation learning to output-driven drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Graph-based deep learning has emerged as a powerful framework for modeling drug-target interactions (DTIs), enabling the integration of molecular, structural, and systems-level information within a unified representation. In this review, we survey graph-based DTI models across biomedical network-, sequence/hybrid-, and structure-based paradigms, which form a continuum from large-scale association inference to structure-resolved interaction modeling with increasing mechanistic specificity. Beyond architectural advances, we introduce an output-driven perspective in which models are evaluated acc
papers.summary: This review surveys graph-based deep learning methods for modeling drug-target interactions, covering network-based, sequence/hybrid, and structure-based approaches. The authors introduce an output-driven perspective for evaluating these models, emphasizing practical utility in drug discovery.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer activity of eravacycline in pancreatic cancer via target-based deep learning and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options. In this study, we introduce a target-based deep learning framework to investigate the anticancer activity of eravacycline (Erav), a United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved antibacterial agent previously identified in our work as a potential anticancer candidate through computational screening. We developed a novel two-phase in silico yeast-based prediction model to explore potential mechanisms of action, followed by in vitro and in vivo experimental validation. DNA polymera
papers.summary: This study uses a deep learning framework to identify the FDA-approved antibiotic eravacycline as a potential treatment for pancreatic cancer, and validates its anticancer activity through laboratory experiments. The approach combines computational prediction with experimental testing to repurpose an existing drug for a new therapeutic use.

papers.title: An open-source pipeline for longitudinal single-cell tracking and cell-cycle/migration coupling analysis for neurotherapeutic screening.
papers.abstract: Imaging-based phenotypic assays are widely used in neuroprotection, drug discovery, and neurorepair studies, but long-term, high-throughput time-lapse datasets remain difficult to analyze because of segmentation noise, photobleaching, crowded fields, cell division, and tracking errors. Fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell cycle indicator (FUCCI) reporters enable live visualization of cell-cycle phases, but their integration with migration behaviors remains limited. This study aimed to developed an open workflow for tracking cycle and motility.
papers.summary: This paper presents an open-source computational pipeline that integrates FUCCI cell-cycle reporters with long-term time-lapse imaging to simultaneously track cell division and migration in neurotherapeutic screening. The tool addresses common challenges like segmentation noise and tracking errors, enabling high-throughput analysis of cell-cycle and motility coupling.

papers.title: From Therapeutic Drug to Xenobiotic in Cancer Repurposing: Clozapine Mechanisms, Metabolic Liabilities, and Human-Relevant Translational Approaches.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing represents a rational and resource-efficient strategy to expand the oncological armamentarium by leveraging the established pharmacology, clinical experience, and safety-monitoring frameworks of approved non-oncological agents. Clozapine (CZP), an atypical antipsychotic characterized by broad receptor pharmacology, complex biotransformation, and clinically relevant toxicological liabilities, has emerged as a candidate of interest following preclinical evidence of context-dependent anticancer activity across multiple tumor types. As such, CZP provides an informative case study
papers.summary: This review examines the potential of repurposing the antipsychotic drug clozapine for cancer treatment, highlighting its complex pharmacology and metabolic properties that may contribute to anticancer activity. The authors discuss preclinical evidence across multiple tumor types and emphasize the need for human-relevant translational approaches to assess this drug repurposing strategy.

papers.title: Intelligence on the graph: Graph neural networks for mechanistic drug target discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug discovery is increasingly challenged by rising costs, long development cycles and high attrition rates, with accurate target identification remaining a critical bottleneck. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated transformative potential, the systematic application of graph neural networks (GNNs) to drug target discovery remains underexplored. To address this gap, this paper provides a comprehensive and structured analysis of recent advances in GNN-based methods for drug-target interaction (DTI) and drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction. We dissect the methodological founda
papers.summary: This review systematically examines how graph neural networks (GNNs) can improve drug target discovery by predicting drug-target interactions and affinities, addressing a key bottleneck in drug development. It provides a structured analysis of recent GNN-based methods, highlighting their potential to reduce costs and attrition rates in drug discovery pipelines.

papers.title: Advancing Antiviral Design: Integrating Natural Products, Computation and Targeted Delivery.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the role of rapid viral mutation and global connectivity in accelerating viral emergence and spread, emphasising the necessity for expedited and adaptable antiviral drug discovery and development. Despite ongoing efforts to develop effective, low-toxicity therapeutics, the number of antivirals that have achieved clinical approval remains limited. The shortfall is especially significant in developing countries, where access to new antivirals is limited by high prices, few options, import dependence, unstable supply chains and weak purchasing systems. The challe
papers.summary: This review discusses the need for faster and more adaptable antiviral drug development, highlighting the limited number of approved antivirals and access issues in developing countries. It explores integrating natural products, computational methods, and targeted delivery to overcome these challenges.

papers.title: Deep learning for small-molecule drug discovery: From molecular design to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly transforming drug discovery, offering new approaches to accelerate the identification and optimization of therapeutic candidates. Deep learning (DL) methods have shown strong potential for generative modeling and molecular property prediction, enabling the design of compounds with tailored pharmacological profiles. In this review, we synthesize recent AI-driven progress in drug discovery, highlighting both achievements and ongoing challenges. We discuss key technical aspects underpinning DL-based models, including the use of cura
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in deep learning for small-molecule drug discovery, covering generative molecular design and property prediction to accelerate the identification of therapeutic candidates. It highlights key technical aspects and discusses both achievements and ongoing challenges in translating AI-driven approaches from molecular design to clinical applications.

papers.title: Contextual Representation Learning With ResNet Refinement and Deep Classification for Enhanced Drug Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug target interactions (DTIs) plays a pivotal role in drug discovery and repositioning. However, it remains challenging due to the structural complexity of proteins and small-molecule compounds, along with the limited generalisation capability of existing computational approaches. Drug target interaction prediction is important in computer-aided drug design and drug repurposing, especially for complex diseases where multiple targets are involved. This study aims to develop a robust deep learning framework that enhances DTI prediction accuracy by effectively capturing c
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning framework that combines contextual representation learning with ResNet refinement and deep classification to improve the accuracy of drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction. The method addresses challenges from protein and compound structural complexity, aiming to enhance generalization for drug discovery and repurposing.

papers.title: Dynamics-enhanced molecular property prediction guided by deep learning.
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction (MPP) is a key challenge in computational biology and drug discovery. Traditional approaches mostly rely on feature representations yielded from static structures of molecules, ignoring their dynamic nature. The scarcity of dynamics data in public databases and the complexity of learning such high-dimensional data made it more difficult for dynamics-involved studies. Accordingly, we built a series of dynamics datasets for MPP tasks by performing comprehensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on different molecules. In addition, we proposed a dynamically enhance
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of molecular property prediction by incorporating molecular dynamics data, which captures the dynamic behavior of molecules rather than relying solely on static structures. The authors created new dynamics datasets through molecular dynamics simulations and developed a deep learning method that leverages this dynamic information to improve prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Revolutionizing drug discovery from natural products: The roles of artificial intelligence and multi-omics in accelerating innovation.
papers.abstract: Natural products and their derivatives have long been crucial in drug therapy, especially in traditional medicine. However, challenges in screening, isolation, characterization, and optimization have slowed their development in the pharmaceutical industry. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and multi-omics technologies are revitalizing this field. AI offers powerful tools for understanding natural compounds, enhancing molecular representations, and supporting tasks such as binding prediction, drug repurposing, and retrosynthesis. Moreover, generative models are aiding in natur
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence and multi-omics technologies are overcoming traditional challenges in natural product drug discovery, such as screening and optimization. AI enhances molecular representation, binding prediction, drug repurposing, and retrosynthesis, while generative models further accelerate innovation.

papers.title: AI-powered therapeutic aptamer drug discovery: Targeting the CT-domain of CTGF for duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a fatal X-linked disorder, features progressive muscle fibrosis as a key driver of mortality. While CTGF represents a therapeutic target for DMD, its VWC-domain-targeting antibody (FG-3019) failed in clinical trials. Through experimental validation, we identified CT-domain as a superior target domain, as it contributed more fibrosis activity of CTGF than VWC-domain without elevating compensatory TGF-β1 level. Aptamers are synthetic oligonucleotides identified through SELEX, which can specifically bind to flexible protein domains through their unique 3D confor
papers.summary: This study identifies the CT-domain of CTGF as a superior therapeutic target for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) compared to the VWC-domain, which was targeted by a failed antibody. Using AI-powered aptamer discovery, the authors developed aptamers that bind the CT-domain, reducing fibrosis without elevating compensatory TGF-β1 levels, offering a promising new approach for DMD treatment.

papers.title: FlowDock: A unified flow-based framework for flexible protein-ligand docking and binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-ligand complexes and binding affinity is critical for hit identification and optimization for structure-based drug design. Traditional docking simulates binding processes with searching algorithms guided by energy-scoring functions, which are quite computationally expensive and time-intensive. In contrast, deep learning approaches offer a cost-effective alternative, yet often generate conformations with limited physicochemical validity and fail to account for protein flexibility. To address these pitfalls, we propose FlowDock, a multitask framework enhanced by Ba
papers.summary: FlowDock is a new deep learning framework that simultaneously predicts protein-ligand docking poses and binding affinity. It uses a flow-based approach to generate physically valid conformations while accounting for protein flexibility, offering a faster and more accurate alternative to traditional computational docking methods for drug discovery.

papers.title: Thiazole-Derived Dual EGFR/CDK-2 Inhibitors: Rational Design, Synthesis, In Vitro Anticancer Evaluation, Mechanistic Profiling, and Computational Binding Analysis.
papers.abstract: New series of thiazole analogues were designed, synthesized, and tested for their potential anticancer activity. All the synthesized compounds were biologically tested against HCT-116 and MCF-7 cell lines. Compounds 14d, 14h, and 14i were determined to be the most active members in this series against HCT-116 cancer cell lines with a considerable safety profile. The three lead compounds were further investigated for their inhibitory activities against EGFR and CDK-2. Compound 14i exhibited the most potent inhibition, with IC50 values of 0.056 and 0.215 µM against EGFR and CDK-2, respectively,
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of new thiazole-based compounds that inhibit both EGFR and CDK-2, with compound 14i showing the most potent dual inhibition. The lead compounds demonstrated strong anticancer activity against colorectal and breast cancer cell lines with a favorable safety profile.

papers.title: Exploring Biofilm Inhibition Potential of Imidazo-Pyridine Linked Tetrazoles Against Candida albicans: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation With Computational Studies.
papers.abstract: Infectious diseases remain one of the major global health challenges due to their rapid transmission and evolving pathogenic mechanisms. Among them, Candida albicans has emerged as a significant opportunistic antifungal pathogen, which is responsible for biofilm-associated infections. In the present study, a library of new tetrazole bearing imidazo-pyridine molecules (4a-4j) was synthesised and characterised through spectroscopic techniques (1H, 13C and MS) for structural confirmation. Their in vitro antifungal potential was evaluated against C. albicans, where compound 4d emerged as the most
papers.summary: This study synthesized and tested a new library of imidazo-pyridine linked tetrazole compounds against Candida albicans, identifying compound 4d as the most potent inhibitor of biofilm formation. The work combines chemical synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational modeling to explore potential new antifungal agents.

papers.title: BoltzOmics: Predicting genetic variant effects on drug binding with Boltz-2.
papers.abstract: A mechanistic understanding of how genetic variants alter drug-receptor binding is central to precision medicine, drug response prediction, and drug development. Yet, experimental mutation-drug profiling remains slow and expensive, while existing computational approaches often trade accuracy for scalability. We developed BoltzOmics, an interactive, open-source platform that integrates Boltz-2, a deep learning model for biomolecular structure prediction, to rapidly assess mutation effects on drug binding. Starting from amino acid sequences, the workflow queries databases for genetic variants, g
papers.summary: BoltzOmics is an open-source platform that uses the deep learning model Boltz-2 to predict how genetic variants affect drug-receptor binding from amino acid sequences. It aims to provide a fast and scalable alternative to experimental mutation-drug profiling for precision medicine and drug development.

papers.title: Ubiquitination modifications as central regulators of metabolic dysfunction in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance, progressive pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, and multi-organ metabolic dysregulation. Among various post-translational modifications, ubiquitination has emerged as a central regulator of cellular homeostasis, with E3 ubiquitin ligases and deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) governing the stability and activity of key signaling proteins. This review systematically elucidates the pivotal role of ubiquitination in the pathogenesis of T2DM. We first outline the fundamental principles of the ubiqui
papers.summary: This review highlights how ubiquitination—a process that tags proteins for degradation—regulates key signaling proteins involved in insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes. It systematically describes the roles of E3 ubiquitin ligases and deubiquitinating enzymes in metabolic dysregulation, suggesting that targeting these enzymes could offer new therapeutic strategies for T2DM.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in drug discovery: from algorithmic foundations to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is quietly reconfiguring the landscape of drug discovery. It sharpens the search for new targets, refines lead compounds, and helps tailor clinical trial designs. Behind these advances sits a family of methods-convolutional, recurrent, and graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and Transformers-that has found its way into every stage of the pipeline. Tasks that once demanded years of trial and error, from pulling meaningful features out of molecules to predicting drug-target affinity and crystal structures wit
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI methods—including convolutional, graph neural networks, transformers, and generative models—are being applied across the drug discovery pipeline, from target identification to clinical trial design. It highlights how these techniques accelerate tasks like molecular feature extraction, drug-target affinity prediction, and structure prediction that previously required years of trial and error.

papers.title: Identification of key targets driving biofilm formation and virtual screening of potential inhibitors in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a member of the "ESKAPE" pathogens, possesses a robust ability to form biofilms-a key factor that contributes to its antibiotic resistance and poses significant challenges for clinical management. Identifying potential therapeutic targets through bioinformatic analysis of genomic data is therefore critical for developing more effective treatment strategies.
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatic analysis of genomic data from Pseudomonas aeruginosa to identify key genes driving biofilm formation, a major contributor to its antibiotic resistance. The researchers then performed virtual screening to find potential inhibitors targeting these genes, offering new avenues for therapeutic development against this difficult-to-treat pathogen.

papers.title: SPPIPred: Stacking-based ensemble learning model for identification of protein-protein interaction.
papers.abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are essential for various biological functions and are crucial in drug discovery, signaling pathways, and network reconstruction. This study presents SPPIPred, an advanced machine learning-based model designed for precise PPI prediction. The SPPIPred model was constructed using five feature extraction methods: Pseudo amino acid composition (PAAC), Composition transition distribution (CTDC), Dipeptide composition (DPC), Word2Vec, and FastText. Among these, FastText emerged as the most effective for encoding protein sequences. Despite the application of featur
papers.summary: SPPIPred is a new machine learning model that predicts protein-protein interactions by combining five different feature extraction methods, with FastText being the most effective. The model uses a stacking-based ensemble learning approach to improve prediction accuracy.

papers.title: AI-driven drug discovery using transformer-based molecular representation learning.
papers.abstract: The vast majority of chemically plausible, drug-like molecules remain unexplored due to the combinatorial scale of chemical space and the limited throughput of experimental screening. This is complicated by the lack of data and the inability to extrapolate predictive models to chemotypes that are not represented well. We introduce a transformer-based molecular modeling framework for target-specific potency prediction, trained on curated BindingDB bioactivity data across Alzheimer's, diabetes, and cancer targets to deliver accurate pIC50 regression and binary activity classification. It uses cu
papers.summary: This paper presents a transformer-based AI framework that predicts drug potency (pIC50) and activity classification for specific targets, trained on curated bioactivity data from BindingDB for Alzheimer's, diabetes, and cancer. The model aims to address the challenge of exploring vast chemical space by enabling accurate predictions even for underrepresented chemotypes, potentially accelerating drug discovery.

papers.title: Recent applications of artificial intelligence in cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy: current status and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) enhances the precision, personalization, and efficiency of cancer treatment through deep learning and machine learning techniques. This review comprehensively examines the evolution of AI and its expanding applications in cancer radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and drug discovery and repurposing. In radiotherapy, AI enables automated medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating the accurate delineation of tumor targets. Furthermore, AI-driven feedback systems support clinicians in developing individualized treatment plans by offering real-time assessment of treatme
papers.summary: This review explores how artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning and machine learning, is improving cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy by enhancing precision, personalization, and efficiency. Key applications include automated tumor segmentation in medical images and AI-driven feedback systems for real-time treatment plan adjustments.

papers.title: In silico identification of novel PTP1B inhibitors by the investigation of molecular mechanism, QSAR, and DFT studies.
papers.abstract: Protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) is a well-known and promising drug target involved in the negative regulation of insulin and leptin signaling, and new anti-diabetic molecules for the treatment of type 2 diabetes are directly in its hands. A series of PTP1B inhibitors was discovered and characterized using in silico techniques, including virtual screening, molecular docking, ADMET profiling, toxicity prediction, VEGA-QSAR analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. A starting library of 1000 anti-diabetic compounds was screened, and Pu
papers.summary: This study used computational methods to identify potential new inhibitors of PTP1B, a key drug target for type 2 diabetes. By screening a library of 1000 anti-diabetic compounds, the researchers found several promising candidates through virtual screening, molecular docking, and other in silico analyses.

papers.title: Multi-Target Cardioprotective Potential of Ajuga bracteosa Phytochemicals: An Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Approach.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI), especially its adrenaline-induced myocardial injury, remains a leading cause of global mortality, often resulting in irreversible cardiac damage and heart failure due to stress cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to identify phytochemicals from Ajuga bracteosa that may protect against adrenaline-induced myocardial infarction by targeting multiple cardiac pathways. The findings suggest that these natural compounds could offer a multi-target therapeutic approach for stress cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Synthesis, characterization, and in vitro and in silico antibacterial evaluation of 5-(3-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amine.
papers.abstract: This study reports the synthesis, structural characterization, and antibacterial evaluation of 5-(3-nitrophenyl)-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amine (NPTA), a commercially available thiadiazole derivative with potential antimicrobial activity.
papers.summary: This study synthesized and characterized a thiadiazole derivative (NPTA) and tested its antibacterial activity in the lab and via computer simulations. The compound showed potential as an antimicrobial agent, but the work is preliminary and focused on a single molecule.

papers.title: Computational and experimental evaluation of Pisolithus arhizus metabolites targeting major efflux pumps of mastitis-associated Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in pathogenic bacteria, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, is an increasing global concern in veterinary medicine. The present study evaluated bioactive metabolites from P. arhizus as potential inhibitors of major S. aureus efflux pumps. The methanolic extracts of P. arhizus were profiled using GC-MS to identify the main constituents, and their antibacterial activity against S. aureus was evaluated using a well diffusion assay. The experimental results showed that the crude methanolic extract exhibited a 20 mm zone of inhibition with a MIC of 30 µg/mL. Furthermo
papers.summary: This study identifies bioactive compounds from the fungus Pisolithus arhizus that can inhibit efflux pumps in drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, a major cause of mastitis in livestock. Using GC-MS profiling and lab experiments, the crude extract showed strong antibacterial activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 30 µg/mL. The findings suggest fungal metabolites as a potential source for new treatments against antimicrobial resistance in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: Targeting PKLR and lipogenic enzymes through JNK inhibition to develop a therapeutic strategy for MASLD and MASH.
papers.abstract: Pyruvate kinase liver and red blood cells (PKLR) is linked to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Previous study, we identified JNK-IN-5A, a c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) inhibitor that suppresses PKL expression in HepG2 cells using computational drug repurposing and screened out four hit JNK-IN-5A derivatives (SET-151, SET-152, SET-162, SET-130).
papers.summary: This study identifies JNK-IN-5A and its derivatives as potential therapeutics for MASLD/MASH by suppressing PKLR and lipogenic enzyme expression. The findings suggest a new strategy targeting metabolic pathways in liver disease.

papers.title: Tissue-autonomous pharmacological direction: how target expression landscapes convert balanced compounds into tissue-selective agents.
papers.abstract: Multi-target drugs frequently exhibit tissue-dependent pharmacological directions: the same compound may promote a biological process in one organ while driving its functional opposite in another. Tamoxifen antagonizes estrogen receptors in breast tissue yet activates them in the endometrium; non-selective NSAIDs reduce inflammation at injury sites while damaging the gastric mucosa. Each phenomenon has been explained by drug-specific mechanisms, but no unifying principle predicts when or why such direction reversal occurs. Here we propose tissue-autonomous pharmacological direction (TAPD): whe
papers.summary: This paper proposes a unifying principle called tissue-autonomous pharmacological direction (TAPD) to explain why multi-target drugs can have opposite effects in different tissues, such as tamoxifen acting as an antagonist in breast tissue but an agonist in the endometrium. The authors suggest that the expression landscape of drug targets across tissues determines whether a balanced compound will become tissue-selective, potentially enabling better prediction of drug side effects and therapeutic outcomes.
